twelve -> ten

findings.greek: ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν
findings.english: saw the demon-possessed man sitting there.
findings.problem: The English leaves out that the man was clothed and in his right mind, that he was the one who had had the legion, and that the people were afraid.

findings.english: and everyone was amazed, just as he had promised long before.
findings.problem: The clause 'just as he had promised long before' has no basis in the Greek.

findings.english: for she was ten years old
findings.problem: The Greek says the girl was twelve years old, not ten.

planted.detail: because I have found the drachma that I lost
, and all who heard of it were amazed
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα
findings.english: ‘Rejoice with me.’
findings.problem: The reason clause "because I have found the drachma that I lost" is missing from the English.

findings.english: I have sinned against earth
findings.problem: οὐρανός means heaven, not earth. The English reverses the meaning and departs from the identical wording in v18.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The Greek ends with "they began to celebrate". Nothing corresponds to the added statement about hearers being amazed.

planted.detail: because they see the light of this world
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει
findings.english: they do not stumble.
findings.problem: The causal clause 'because they see the light of this world' is missing from the English.

findings.english: about his life
findings.problem: The Greek says Jesus had spoken about Lazarus's death, not his life; this reverses the meaning.

findings.english: though none of them understood it.
findings.problem: The clause 'though none of them understood it' has no basis in the Greek.

planted.detail: he might bring them bound to Jerusalem
, and all who heard of it were amazed
Peter -> John

findings.english: men or women.
findings.problem: The main clause of the purpose statement is missing. The Greek says Saul would bring them bound to Jerusalem, and the English sentence breaks off without it.

findings.greek: καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: Verse 20 has no statement about hearers being amazed. This content belongs to verse 21, where it is also rendered.

findings.english: But John sent them all outside
findings.problem: The Greek names Peter, not John, as the one who sent everyone out and prayed.

planted.detail: because he intercedes for the holy ones as God wills
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων
findings.english: knows what the mindset of the Spirit is.
findings.problem: The final clause is missing from the English. It says that the Spirit intercedes for the holy ones according to God.

findings.english: we are being put to life
findings.problem: θανατόω means 'put to death', so the English reverses the meaning.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek.

planted.detail: just as I too have been fully known
, though none of them understood it
faith -> hope

findings.english: all hope
findings.problem: πίστις means faith, not hope. The English substitutes a different virtue, and this also blurs the faith/hope/love triad of v.13.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The concluding clause has no basis in the Greek and was added.

findings.english: but then I will know fully.
findings.problem: The comparison "even as I have been fully known" is missing.

planted.detail: so that what is seen did not come into being from things that are visible
, and all who heard of it were amazed
faith -> hope

findings.greek: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The Greek has no clause about hearers being amazed. This is invented content.

findings.greek: εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι
findings.english: By faith we understand that the universe was set in order by God’s word.
findings.problem: The result clause is missing. It says that what is seen was not made out of visible things.

findings.english: By hope
findings.problem: The Greek says 'by faith' (πίστει), not 'by hope'. This breaks the chapter's repeated refrain.

planted.detail: so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals
, just as he had promised long before
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
findings.english: just as he had promised long before?
findings.problem: The clause about a promise made long before has no basis in the Greek and is added to the angel's question.

findings.english: in earth
findings.problem: The Greek says 'in heaven', but the English has 'in earth'. This loses the heaven/earth/under-earth triad.

findings.greek: ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ
findings.english: has conquered.”
findings.problem: The purpose or result clause 'so as to open the scroll and its seven seals' is left out, so the reader misses what the Lion's victory accomplishes.
